meta.title: Manitoba Historical Tornado-System Simulator
meta.subtitle: Executive Stakeholder Edition
meta.purpose: Compare an unfolding storm against Manitoba's worst on record — so responders can size what's coming.

confirmed.label: Confirmed
confirmed.blurb: Verified by an official damage survey. Sourced from Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) and the Northern Tornadoes Project (NTP).

historical_estimate.label: Historical estimate
historical_estimate.blurb: A real recorded loss, adjusted for inflation into 2026 dollars. Shown as a likely range because inflation-normalization carries uncertainty.

projection.label: Projection
projection.blurb: A computer-modelled estimate, not yet observed — always shown with its likely range rather than a single number. The range spans the 10th to 90th percentile (P10–P90) of 100,000 simulated outcomes; the central estimate is the 50th percentile (P50).

strainMethodology.label: analytical proxy
strainMethodology.oneLiner: How hard this storm pushed emergency crews, scored 0–100.
strainMethodology.plain: The Emergency-Resource Strain Index is a single 0–100 score that estimates how hard an event pushed on emergency resources. It blends four plain things: how many warnings were issued and for how long, the peak number of customers without power, how many municipalities were hit, and casualties (deaths weighted heavily). Each piece is scored as a share of the worst value seen across these five events, then averaged. 100 = the heaviest strain in this roster; it is a comparison tool, not an exact measurement.

events.name: Elie F5 — June 2007 Outbreak
events.headline: Canada's only officially rated F5 tornado. It flattened homes in Elie yet, remarkably, killed no one.

timeline.label: Severe thunderstorm intensifies west of Elie
Tornado touches down; first home destroyed
Peak intensity — a house is lifted off its foundation
Track turns east through the edge of town
Tornado lifts; no fatalities recorded

duration.source: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) / Northern Tornadoes Project (NTP) survey

events.name: Alonsa EF4 — August 2018
events.headline: A violent EF4 near Lake Manitoba. The only fatality among these five events occurred here.

timeline.label: Tornado-warned supercell develops near Alonsa
Tornado touches down south of the community
Peak EF4 intensity strikes seasonal homes
Track moves northeast toward Lake Manitoba
Tornado dissipates; one fatality confirmed

duration.source: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) / Northern Tornadoes Project (NTP) survey

recordedDamage.value: Homes & cottages destroyed near Margaret Bruce Beach

events.name: June 2023 — Three Confirmed Tornadoes
events.headline: A multi-tornado afternoon across south-central Manitoba; three tornadoes were confirmed by survey.

timeline.label: Supercells fire along a southern Manitoba boundary
First tornado confirmed near Carman (EF2)
Second tornado near Miami (EF1)
Third tornado near Manitou (EF1)
Storms weaken; surveys later confirm three tornadoes

duration.source: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) / Northern Tornadoes Project (NTP) survey

events.name: June 2, 2026 — Three EF0 Tornadoes
events.headline: A weak-tornado day: three short-lived EF0s touched down with minimal damage.

timeline.label: Marginal supercells develop near the U.S. border
Brief EF0 touchdown near Winkler (RM of Stanley)
Second EF0 near Altona (RM of Rhineland)
Third EF0 in the RM of Montcalm
Activity ends; all three rated EF0 by survey

duration.source: Environment and Climate Change Canada (ECCC) / Northern Tornadoes Project (NTP) survey

recordedDamage.value: Minor — tree limbs and crop damage

events.name: June 9, 2026 — Survey Pending
events.headline: Damage survey pending — figures below are projections. A hail-dominated event across the Interlake east of Winnipeg.
events.pendingBanner: Damage survey pending — no confirmed tornado count yet. Every figure for this event is a modeled projection shown with its likely range.

timeline.label: Severe storms build over the Interlake (modeled)
Giant hail reported; outages begin to climb (modeled)
Peak ~13,250 Manitoba Hydro customers without power (estimated from power-outage data)
Storms exit east; ground survey not yet completed
